question:
A 88-year-old male presents with sudden-onset pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath. He denies
fever, chills, cough, or lower-extremity swelling. His medical history includes prostate cancer, type 2
diabetes, chronic renal insufficiency (baseline serum creatinine: 2.6 mg/dL), an estimated glomerular
filtration rate of 24 mL/min/1.73 m², and treated hypertension. He recently underwent surgery for a
pathologic hip fracture. On examination, his respiratory rate is 21 breaths per minute, oxygen
saturation is 89% on room air, heart rate is 104 beats per minute, and blood pressure is 115/83 mm Hg.
His lungs are clear, and there are no cardiac murmurs or rubs. Surgical incisions are well healed, and
there is no lower-extremity edema. Testing for SARS-CoV-2 is negative, and a chest radiograph shows

no opacities. Laboratory results include serum sodium of 134 mEq/L, serum creatinine of 2.8 mg/dL,
and a leukocyte count of 7800/mm³. Which of the following diagnostic tests is the most appropriate next
step for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Exercise stress test (B) D-dimer test (C) Chest MRI with
contrast (D) CT angiogram of the chest (E) Transthoracic echocardiogram (F) Ventilation-perfusion
imaging (G) Lower extremity duplex ultrasound (H) High-resolution chest CT (I) Arterial blood gas
analysis (J) D-dimer testing
 A. Transthoracic echocardiogram
B. D-dimer testing
C. Chest MRI with contrast
D. Exercise stress test
E. CT angiogram of the chest
F. High-resolution chest CT
G. Arterial blood gas analysis
H. Lower extremity duplex ultrasound
I. D-dimer test
J. Ventilation-perfusion imaging
